assertions.evidence: | Scenario | Shipping Method | Order Value | Destination | Free Express Threshold (Policy) | Cost? |

assertions.text: Express shipping is split into at least two cases distinguishing the UK free tier (UK, order £50+, free) from the paid tier. The split is driven by the UK-only free threshold rule.

Express rows use value sets to consolidate cases with the same outcome — e.g. non-UK destinations at/above threshold in one row (such as {Ireland, Other} or {Ireland, International}), or UK at/above threshold in one row ({£50, £75}). Not enumerated as separate rows per destination or per order value when the result is identical. Any reasonable label for non-UK/Ireland destinations is acceptable (International, Other, Rest of World, etc.).
assertions.evidence: Separate rows for 'Express | £50.00 | UK | £50.00 | £0.00' and 'Express | £75.00 | UK | £50.00 | £0.00' should consolidate to {£50, £75}

assertions.text: Overnight UK and Ireland are in one row using a value set ({UK, Ireland}) — not separate rows, since both have the same cost and availability.
assertions.evidence: 'Overnight to UK' and 'Overnight to Ireland' are separate rows, not consolidated in one row with {UK, Ireland}

assertions.text: Standard shipping destination uses a value set covering all options (e.g. {UK, Ireland, International} or {UK, Ireland, Other}) or is blank/absent — either approach is valid since destination is irrelevant to the cost. Any reasonable label for non-UK/Ireland destinations is acceptable.
At least one output column ends with '?'
Cell values use concrete domain terms (e.g. 'Standard', 'Express', 'UK', '£3.99') — not abstract codes or raw booleans like 'true', 'false', 'TYPE_1', '1'.

Value sets (not blanks) are used for irrelevant inputs — e.g. Standard shipping destination uses a value set like {UK, Ireland, International} because destination exists but doesn't affect the cost. Blanks are reserved for genuinely absent/N/A inputs. The distinction between 'irrelevant to this rule' (value set) and 'not applicable' (blank) is correct.
assertions.evidence: Policy column blank for 'Standard' and 'Overnight' rows (N/A), filled with '£50.00' for Express rows (policy setting)

assertions.text: Multiple tables (or @TableTest methods) are used, each addressing a distinct concern — not one monolithic table mixing unrelated rules. Acceptable to use a single table only when the domain genuinely has a single concern.
assertions.evidence: Author states 'Two distinct concerns here: what shipping options are available, and what they cost' but only one table is provided

assertions.text: Each table has only the rows needed to express its concern's rules — no unnecessary permutations from combining concerns. Fewer rows per table is expected when concerns are properly separated.
assertions.evidence: 'Overnight not available internationally' provides availability info, unnecessary in cost table if availability was separated

assertions.text: Shipping method availability and shipping cost are in separate tables
assertions.evidence: Single table 'Shipping Cost Calculation' contains both costs ('£14.99') and availability ('Not available') in Cost column
